subject: Re: MedSys — routing decoupling / SCCs vs UK Addendum discovery
messages:
From: Sara Bell <sara.bell@medsys.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial scope questions — routing + UK Addendum + evidence split

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for taking time this week. As we discussed on the call, MedSys is preparing the TIA packet and we need to understand how Redwood intends to handle international routing where the processing will be: 
- UK resident PHI tokenization + onshore model inference (UK Addendum territory), and
- EU-hosted analytics fallback (SCCs route) for aggregated telemetry.

Specific asks:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood classifies the two paths as separate subprocessors or as a single processor with regional routing?
2) What evidence will you provide for the UK IDTA addendum vs the SCCs evidence bucket (we need mapping to our template columns)?
3) Any known constraints with prefix/KV caching when traffic is split by region — does that create additional cross-border footprints we should capture?

I've attached our draft TIA scope (MedSys_TIA_Scope.xlsx). We'd like a 45‑minute working session next week to walk through a mapping, and ideally a short pre-read from your side that maps Redwood artifacts to our TIA columns so our privacy team can validate.

Proposed windows (BST preferred): Tue 02 Jun 14:00–15:00 / Wed 03 Jun 10:00–10:45. Procurement will also want to attend on the mapping call.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Bell
Senior Privacy Manager — MedSys Health
privacy@medsys.com
Attachments: MedSys_TIA_Scope.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bell <sara.bell@medsys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial scope questions — routing + UK Addendum + evidence split

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Happy to run the mapping session and bring the artifacts. High level answers up front so your team can prep:

- Processor model: Redwood treats the serving runtime as a single logical processor with regional execution variants. We model regional clusters as "execution zones" that can be recorded as subprocessors in your spreadsheet where customers require zone-level attestations. In practice, for UK‑Addendum customers we present the UK cluster as a bounded subprocessors set (VM images, KMS envelope) and supply the IDTA mapping.

- Evidence split: we'll supply an evidence bundle per legal regime. For SCCs we provide the standard controls export (subprocessor list, encryption-in-transit/at-rest, subprocessors by region). For the UK Addendum we'll include the IDTA appendix, the UK addendum signature page, and a short control narrative documenting key routing safeguards. I'll attach our Redwood_Evidence_Map.pdf as a pre-read.

- KV/prefix cache: caching is per execution zone by design. If traffic is split and a request is routed across zones (failover/fallback), ephemeral KV artifacts are kept only in the zone that served the token and TTLs are scoped to the zone. That said, if you need a formal statement we can include a cache-residency section in the evidence pack.

Let's schedule Tue 02 Jun 14:00 BST (which is 06:00 PDT). Is that OK for your procurement folks? If not, suggest Wed 03 Jun 10:00 BST.

Attaching: Redwood_Evidence_Map.pdf (6 pages).

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Evidence_Map.pdf (6 pages)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Bell <sara.bell@medsys.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 12:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial scope questions — routing + UK Addendum + evidence split

Sara, Rafael — quick technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective that I will cover in the mapping call:

- Routing policy: we support policy-based routing (region priority, cost tier, fallback). For MedSys we recommend a strict-region policy for UK‑resident PHI to avoid cross-border failover unless you opt-in to fallback.

- Subprocessor boundaries: the "UK cluster" is comprised of a set of managed instances + a regional cache tier. We can provide a concise list of instance images and third-party monitoring/metrics processors (these would be listed as subprocessors in the UK evidence bucket).

- Audit logs & retention: logs for UK zone are retained per your retention request — default 90 days, can be extended. We will provide sample audit snippets (redacted) showing request routing headers that prove locality.

I'll prepare a one‑page tech slide for the pre-read and add a section on cache residency and failover semantics so you have a formal statement to include in your TIA.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security — Redwood Inference
Attachments: UK_Addendum_Checklist.pdf (2 pages)

From: Sara Bell <sara.bell@medsys.com>

Thanks Rafael and Kim — that level of detail is perfect. Procurement confirms Tue 02 Jun 14:00 BST works for us (I booked a Teams invite and added procurement@medsys.com). We appreciate the pre-read — if you can include the short cache-residency statement + a redacted audit example that traces a UK‑resident request end-to-end, that will speed review.

Could you also include a short note on whether any of your subprocessors for the UK cluster are US-based (we need that listed explicitly in our column C)? If yes, please flag the role (e.g., monitoring, build pipeline) and whether data is transferred to that subprocessor.

Looking forward to the call.

Sara
Sara Bell
Senior Privacy Manager — MedSys Health
